title: Canada Visa Waits From India Hold Steady: Work Permits 10 Weeks, Study Permits 8 Weeks
excerpt: IRCC's November 12 update left India's work and study permit estimates unchanged, edged visitor visas up to 34 days and super visas to 87 days, and moved waits mainly for Pakistan, the Philippines and in-Canada filings.
body:
• For applicants in India, Canada's headline waits did not move in IRCC's November 12 update: work permits stay at 10 weeks and study permits at 8 weeks.
  • Two India figures did edge up: visitor visas rose two days to 34 days, and super visas for parents and grandparents rose two days to 87 days.
  • The bigger moves were elsewhere — work permit waits rose a week for Pakistan and the Philippines, while study permits filed inside Canada fell two weeks to 6 weeks, their fastest in over four months.
  • IRCC's next temporary-residence update is expected around November 18. Check your own figure in the official IRCC processing-times tool before booking travel or a job start date.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) released updated processing-time estimates on November 13, reflecting figures as of November 12, 2026. For the applicants this site's readers ask about most — those filing from India — the update is mostly a story of no change, with two small increases on family-visit routes.

What it means if you are applying from India

A work permit application from India is estimated at 10 weeks, unchanged from the November 4 figures. A study permit from India is estimated at 8 weeks, also unchanged, according to CIC News, which compared the November 12 release with the previous week's. The two India figures that did move were visitor visas, up two days to 34 days, and super visas — the multi-entry visa for parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens and permanent residents — up two days to 87 days, against a service standard of 112 days.

Where the waits actually rose and fell

The headline changes in this update landed on other countries and on in-Canada filings. Work permit waits rose by one week for applicants in Pakistan, to 10 weeks — the slowest for Pakistan since late August — and by one week for the Philippines, also to 10 weeks, a level not seen in more than five months. Work permits filed inside Canada held at 16 weeks.

Study permits moved the other way. Applications filed inside Canada dropped two weeks, to 6 weeks, and applications from Pakistan dropped one week, to 4 weeks — both the fastest pace in more than four months. Visitor visa extensions from inside Canada eased from 310 days to 304 days. Super visa waits fell sharply for Pakistan, down 10 days to 91 days, and fell five days each for Nigeria and the Philippines.

How to read these numbers

IRCC's processing times are estimates of how long a decision may take after a complete application is submitted. They are not guarantees and not maximums. Some are calculated from how long 80 percent of recent applications took; others are forward-looking, based on the department's current inventory and processing capacity. Service standards are different again: they are IRCC's own targets — 120 days for in-Canada work and study permit submissions, 60 days for submissions from outside Canada, and 14 days for visitor visas from outside Canada.

IRCC generally updates temporary-residence processing times weekly. Between January and August 2026 it finalised 2,076,745 temporary residence applications, with a further 365,425 still in its inventory as of August 31. The next update is expected around November 18. If you are timing a course start, a job start or a parent's visit, use the IRCC processing-times tool for your exact application type and country on the day you file — the figure for another country or category does not describe your file.
